editorial.headline: The Wider Health Workforce, Clearly Classified
editorial.standfirst: Health services beyond doctors and dentists are nationally open to full foreign ownership, with Bali remaining unblocked under its risk-based moratorium reading.
editorial.body:
Health-service work does not begin and end with a doctor’s consultation. This activity covers the delivery of health services by health personnel other than doctors and dentists. Its stated scope is deliberately broad: nursing, midwifery, pharmacy, public-health and environmental-health work sit alongside nutrition, physical therapy, medical technical work and biomedical engineering. It also names traditional-health personnel, clinical psychologists, physiotherapists and other health workers. The distinction matters because the scope is framed around the health personnel who provide the service, while explicitly excluding doctors and dentists from that provider description.

Traditional health is not an afterthought in this definition. The scope expressly includes traditional health services delivered by traditional health personnel, and by others with traditional-health competence, in traditional health-service facilities. Griya Sehat is identified as part of that setting and described as a Type 1 Traditional Health Clinic. In editorial terms, this makes it a broad service category with a specific place for traditional-health practice, rather than a label confined to one conventional profession. The record preserves that connection between the traditional service and the facility it names.

For a registration, the category is open across Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales. That breadth does not alter its subject: health services performed by the non-doctor, non-dentist health personnel set out in the scope. Nationally, the PMA status is open, with maximum foreign ownership of 100%. The national position is therefore direct: foreign ownership may reach full ownership. The record does not confine the activity to one business size or set a foreign-shareholding ceiling below full ownership.

Bali calls for a scale-aware reading, but not a false note of prohibition. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, island-wide and permanently. For this activity, however, the OSS risk at the Large scale is Medium-High/High; the Bali assessment consequently records it as not blocked by the moratorium. The activity is nationally open to a 100% foreign stake, and the Bali record does not block it under the provincial moratorium. That is the honest Bali result on the supplied record.
